summary: Iter26 (Meetings enhancements) — request→booking link, ICS calendar invites, DRAFT/APPROVE minutes flow — tested end-to-end. Backend: 11/12 pytest pass, 1 skipped (no other-client request in DB to trigger 404). Frontend: booking-from-request dialog is preset (no client select, title prefilled), toast '予約しました。相手に通知しました' fires, request card swaps 'テレビ電話を予約' for the 'テレビ電話: {date}' chip, meetings panel refreshes automatically. Consultant minutes editor: textarea prefilled with DRAFT, save→approve→transcript buttons behave per spec (approve disabled while text differs from saved minutes; approve enabled after save; approval yields '承認済み（顧客に公開中）'). Client (client@finora.co.jp) view: minutes button appears only after approval, shows exact approved text ('編集済み議事録_UI'), no editor, no transcript button. Mobile 390px OK. All test seed data cleaned up (TEST_ meetings deleted, request video_meeting_* fields unset).
critical_code_review_comments: meetings._tell uses `list(await client_user_ids(...))` then appends consultant_id when both=True; the `set(uids)` later removes duplicates so consultant will receive the invite even if they happen to also be a client-linked user, but the notify() call is fed the un-deduped list — cheap dupe risk. Consider deduping before notify() as well.

meetings._ics adds ATTENDEE only for the recipient email; for a group call this is fine (1:1) but note SEQUENCE goes 0 (REQUEST) → 1 (CANCEL). If the same meeting is later rescheduled (currently unsupported), SEQUENCE must increment further per RFC5546.

approve_minutes writes minutes_approved := m['minutes'] snapshot at approval time, which is the desired behaviour ('client keeps seeing last approved version even after edit'); confirmed via test test_edit_after_approve_returns_to_draft_client_sees_old.
meetings.edit_minutes returns 409 when minutes_status is PROCESSING/FAILED/None — verified. Message string references the current status; consider translating for FE toasts.
meetings.transcript uses `await _load(user, mid)` twice (indirectly) — the inner _load loads the doc then it's queried again with find_one({id:...}). Minor perf nit; the doc could be reused.

Preserved from iter25: the cross-tenant scope() bug — main agent stated it's fixed in core.scope. Verified indirectly: consultantb no longer creates meetings referencing tenant A's client_id (test_other_tenant_cannot_create in test_meetings.py now returns 403/404).
